network.overall_strategy: This connected network contains 15 molecule nodes, 12 reaction nodes and 10 distinct feedstock-to-target route variants. The variants share three experimentally supported Asn-forming reaction families; they are not ten independently demonstrated mechanisms. The strongest mechanistically anchored family uses cyanoacetylene, ammonia and HCN to form an aminodinitrile, followed by partial hydrolysis. The target connectivity is HOOC-CH(NH2)-CH2-CONH2, not the reversed monoamide regioisomer. Alternative target-forming edges represent Asn detection in reduced-gas spark experiments and alanine/formamide contact-glow experiments. Their atom-balanced equations are formal product-channel balances, not experimentally closed material balances, established elementary mechanisms or measurements of H2 evolution. Explicit coefficients are recorded in mechanism fields rather than by repeating molecule IDs. All environments are anoxic. Atmospheric energy processing and subsequent aqueous collection are represented within Surface; prolonged hot hydrothermal residence is not introduced because it would aggravate Asn loss. Numerical conditions not supplied by the cited research are explicitly identified as proposed screening conditions, not validated synthesis optima. Boundary delivery of a molecule is permitted even when another pathway produces it internally. Thus HCN, cyanoacetylene, alanine and formamide can be either delivered feedstocks or network products. Concentration, transfer losses and compatibility of crude mixtures remain unvalidated integration requirements. Net accumulation must satisfy formation flux greater than measured hydrolytic, photochemical and transport losses; no accumulation yield is claimed without those measurements. Aspartic acid is included only as a degradation sink and uses the schema's intermediate role because no byproduct role is available. Direct Asp amidation is excluded as unvalidated. The 243 K meteorite/proton experiment of Bizzarri et al. (2026) is not relabeled as warm terrestrial chemistry or encoded as a closed conversion with unknown coproducts.

reactions.name: Reduced-gas energetic production of HCN: formal net source channel

conditions.temperature: 300-370 K bulk gas and 300-310 K collection water, proposed scenario; discharge electrons are nonthermal
conditions.pressure: Approximately 1 bar in the proposed gas-collection system; atmospheric production also depends on altitude
conditions.other: Anoxic CH4/NH3-containing reducing gas exposed to electrical discharge or atmospheric photochemistry. H2 may also be externally supplied as background gas. For the Wogan atmospheric scenario, substantial nitrile rainout requires a sufficiently methane-rich atmosphere, approximately CH4/CO2 > 0.1. Proposed collection uses low-gas-exchange water-filled pores at initial pH 8.5-9.5. Collection efficiency, residence time and accumulated HCN concentration are not established.

reactions.mechanism: Formal atom balance: CH4 + NH3 -> HCN + 3 H2. Energy-driven radical chemistry removes hydrogen while forming a C-N bond. This equation summarizes one possible net source channel and is not an elementary atmospheric reaction or a complete discharge product inventory.
reactions.reasoning: Reduced-gas energetic chemistry supplies cyanide-class precursors, while Wogan et al. (2023) model substantial HCN delivery during particular post-impact reducing episodes; Lemmon (1970) reviews the associated prebiotic nitrile chemistry. Neither source establishes this minimal equation as a measured exclusive conversion. The H2 coefficient closes the formal atom balance and must not be interpreted as measured gas evolution. HCN volatilization, competing reactions and retention during atmospheric cooling remain explicit uncertainties.

reactions.name: Reduced-gas discharge production of cyanoacetylene: formal net source channel

conditions.temperature: 300-370 K bulk gas with nonthermal electrical excitation; proposed receiver at 300-310 K
conditions.pressure: Approximately 1 bar for the proposed discharge-collection analogue
conditions.other: Anoxic reduced-gas processing followed by prompt condensation or dissolution into a cooler reservoir. No mineral catalyst is assumed. The numerical bulk temperatures and pressure are scenario choices, not conditions recovered from the supplied 1966 experimental record. Cyanoacetylene delivery must be measured independently of its subsequent aqueous consumption.

reactions.mechanism: Formal atom balance: 3 CH4 + NH3 -> C3HN + 7 H2. The aggregate channel requires hydrocarbon growth, nitrogen incorporation and dehydrogenation through an unresolved energetic reaction network. H2 is a formal redox-balancing product, not a reported quantitative coproduct.
reactions.reasoning: Cyanoacetylene availability from reduced-gas electrical-discharge chemistry underlies the experiments of Sanchez, Ferris and Orgel (1966), summarized by Lemmon (1970). Wogan et al. (2023) provide a conditional atmospheric source framework rather than validation of this particular lumped equation. This source edge is therefore a balanced aggregate representation, not proof that methane and ammonia selectively produce cyanoacetylene. Capture into a cooler reservoir and sufficient co-concentration with HCN and ammonia are required but unquantified.

reactions.name: Atmospheric acetylene cyanation with hydrogen termination: conditional net source channel

conditions.temperature: 300-350 K bulk gas as a proposed reaction-zone scenario; 300-310 K collection water
conditions.pressure: Altitude-dependent atmospheric pressure; approximately 1 bar at the surface receiver
conditions.other: Anoxic atmospheric radical chemistry driven by UV or other energetic processing. CN generation occurs in the atmosphere, not by assuming that short-wavelength atmospheric photolysis proceeds inside a sheltered pond. The model does not specify a measured conversion time or terrestrial collection yield for this complete net channel.

reactions.mechanism: Formal atom balance: C2H2 + HCN -> C3HN + H2. A candidate decomposition is HCN photodissociation to CN and H, addition of CN to acetylene with H elimination, and hydrogen-atom recombination. The net balance assumes this CN source and termination route; it is not itself elementary.
reactions.reasoning: Wogan et al. (2023) explicitly include C2H2 + CN -> HCCCN + H in atmospheric cyanoacetylene production. The full HCN-to-CN and H-to-H2 closure used here is a conditional mechanistic reduction, not a separately demonstrated pond synthesis. It supplies a chemically distinct cyanoacetylene source without adding arbitrary mineral catalysts. Atmospheric attenuation, competing CN reactions and transport into cooler water remain limitations.

reactions.name: Ammonia addition to cyanoacetylene

conditions.other: Proposed initial conditions: pH 8.5-9.5, 1-50 mM cyanoacetylene and 10-200 mM total ammonia/ammonium; sample over 1 hour to 7 days. These concentrations, pH values and sampling times are experimental design ranges, not reported optimum conditions. Use low-gas-exchange, optically sheltered pores after atmospheric delivery; monitor volatilization and competing oligomerization.

reactions.mechanism: Atom balance: C3HN + NH3 -> C3H4N2. Nucleophilic ammonia addition to the activated alkyne, followed by proton transfer, gives NC-CH=CH-NH2. No specific alkene stereochemistry is asserted.
reactions.reasoning: This addition is part of the cyanoacetylene/ammonia/HCN sequence proposed by Sanchez, Ferris and Orgel (1966) and summarized by Lemmon (1970). The supplied evidence supports the overall Asn-producing chemistry more strongly than the isolation, yield and kinetics of every intermediate. Ammonia is a reactant, not an added mineral catalyst. The proposed numerical window requires testing because dilute open water may lose the reagents faster than productive chemistry consumes them.

reactions.name: HCN addition to the aminoacrylonitrile system

conditions.other: Proposed initial pH 8.0-9.5 with 1-50 mM aminoacrylonitrile and 1-100 mM total HCN/cyanide; sample over 1 hour to 7 days. These are unvalidated screening conditions. Retain the solution in sheltered low-gas-exchange pores and quantify cyanide loss and oligomer formation. No enantioselective agent is assumed.

reactions.mechanism: Atom balance: C3H4N2 + HCN -> C4H5N3. Enamine-imine interconversion permits cyanide addition to an imine/iminium-like carbon and proton transfer, giving NC-CH2-CH(NH2)-CN. The chiral center is formed without a demonstrated stereochemical preference.
reactions.reasoning: The aminodinitrile is the proposed recognizable precursor in the Sanchez, Ferris and Orgel (1966) sequence as discussed by Lemmon (1970). The cited evidence does not establish an independently optimized rate law or stereoselective synthesis for this edge. Co-location of HCN with the aminoacrylonitrile and competition from HCN oligomer chemistry are substantive requirements, not consequences of assigning both reactions to Surface.

reactions.name: Partial aminodinitrile hydrolysis to the correct Asn regioisomer
agents: Hydronium as a general-acid catalyst in volcanically acidified water

conditions.temperature: 323-353 K during proposed hydrolysis screening; prompt cooling to 300-310 K afterward
conditions.catalyst: Aqueous hydronium; no mineral catalyst assumed
conditions.other: Proposed initial screen: 1-20 mM aminodinitrile, pH 2.0-3.0, with samples at 0.25, 1, 6, 24 and 72 hours. Volcanic HCl-bearing water is a possible anoxic acidity source. Record pH drift as ammonia is released. These are not published optimum conditions. Measure dinitrile, both monoamide regioisomers, Asn and Asp; transfer into cooler pH 5.5-7.0 water only if an Asn maximum is observed. Residence time must be determined experimentally.

reactions.mechanism: Atom balance: C4H5N3 + 3 H2O -> C4H8N2O3 + NH3. The nitrile adjacent to the amino-bearing carbon must reach the carboxylic-acid state, while the remote nitrile stops at the carboxamide state, producing HOOC-CH(NH2)-CH2-CONH2. This is an aggregate hydrolysis edge; it does not assert a uniquely established hydration order or isolated sequence of amide intermediates.
reactions.reasoning: Sanchez, Ferris and Orgel (1966), summarized by Lemmon (1970), support Asn/Asp production through this precursor family; the historical approximately 10% figure is not a demonstrated isolated Asn yield for the proposed conditions. The key unresolved issues are positional selectivity and interception before deamidation. Glavin et al. (2024) motivate prompt cooling and avoidance of prolonged hot-water exposure. For kinetic evaluation, an explicitly provisional model is d[D]/dt = -kf[D] and d[Asn]/dt = phi*kf[D] - kloss[Asn], where phi includes correct-regioisomer selectivity. kf, phi and kloss must be measured; no favorable values are assumed.

reactions.name: Miller-type Asn detection: atom-balanced observational macroedge

conditions.temperature: 353 K water reservoir in the reported experiment; nonthermal discharge zone and separately cooled condensate
conditions.pressure: Closed gas-circulation apparatus; exact operating pressure is not specified in the supplied research
conditions.other: Reported setup: 125 mL water, CH4/NH3/H2 gas inventory, tungsten-electrode discharge for 3 or 7 days, and twice-daily CH4/NH3 replenishment. Tungsten electrodes deliver energy and are not assigned a catalytic role. H2 is also an externally supplied background gas. Solution pH, gas partial pressures and discharge power are not supplied and are not invented here. Cool and shield collected products rather than assuming indefinite survival in the warm reservoir.

reactions.mechanism: Formal product-channel balance: 4 CH4 + 2 NH3 + 3 H2O -> C4H8N2O3 + 10 H2. This conserves atoms but is not the measured overall apparatus reaction. Asn arises within an unresolved gas-liquid radical and nitrile network. The H2 term is formal bookkeeping and neither establishes H2 evolution nor identifies actual coproduct proportions.
reactions.reasoning: Jiang et al. (2014) directly detected Asn in reduced-gas discharge mixtures and reported its high relative abundance in the three-day condensate, but did not establish a unique Asn mechanism or an absolute carbon yield. This observational macroedge is deliberately distinguished from the mechanistic nitrile sequence. Wogan et al. (2023) support transient strongly reducing episodes rather than a permanently methane/ammonia-rich global atmosphere. Natural lightning scaling, repeated reagent replenishment and product survival remain unresolved.

reactions.name: Acetaldehyde Strecker formation of alanine aminonitrile

conditions.other: Proposed initial pH 8.0-9.5, 1-50 mM acetaldehyde, 1-100 mM total HCN/cyanide and 10-200 mM total ammonia/ammonium. Screen 1 hour to 7 days. These are design conditions rather than conditions reported for an integrated Asn synthesis. Acetaldehyde and HCN are volatile; open-pan evaporation is not assumed to retain them quantitatively.

reactions.mechanism: Atom balance: C2H4O + NH3 + HCN -> C3H6N2 + H2O. Carbonyl addition and dehydration generate an imine/iminium system; cyanide addition gives CH3-CH(NH2)-CN. Without asymmetric selection, the product is stereochemically unspecified.
reactions.reasoning: This is the established Strecker reaction class (Strecker, 1850), included as a chemically justified alanine precursor module rather than as an additional independently demonstrated Asn mechanism. The supplied Asn report does not demonstrate this exact module connected to the Munegumi discharge experiment. Delivery of acetaldehyde, retention of cyanide and compatibility of the resulting crude solution with subsequent processing remain unvalidated.

reactions.name: Alanine aminonitrile hydrolysis
agents: Hydronium as a general-acid hydrolysis catalyst

conditions.other: Proposed initial pH 1-2 in volcanically acidified water; screen 1-30 days with measured conversion rather than assume completion. Process before introducing formamide or Asn. Afterward, cool to 300-320 K and assess the feasibility of concentrating alanine to 100 mM. Residual acidity, salts and byproducts must be characterized before any contact-glow step.

reactions.mechanism: Atom balance: C3H6N2 + 2 H2O -> C3H7NO2 + NH3. Acid-catalyzed nitrile hydration followed by amide hydrolysis converts the aminonitrile into alanine. The equation uses neutral molecular bookkeeping; ammonia will predominantly be ammonium in the acidic solution.
reactions.reasoning: Aminonitrile hydrolysis is the established completion step of Strecker amino-acid synthesis (Strecker, 1850). The supplied Asn literature does not establish its rate under the mildest proposed geochemical conditions or demonstrate preparation of a suitable 100 mM alanine feed from such a hydrolysate. Munegumi (2014) supports the later alanine/formamide product observation, not this integrated preparation. Separating hydrolysis from the target-forming stage avoids exposing already formed Asn or formamide to this prolonged acidic heating.

reactions.name: HCN hydration as a conditional formamide supply route
agents: Hydronium as a general-acid hydration catalyst

conditions.pressure: Approximately 1 bar in low-gas-exchange pores or covered reservoirs
conditions.other: Proposed initial pH 2-3 and 1-100 mM HCN, sampled over 1-30 days. These are unvalidated supply conditions, not an established production protocol. Quantify volatilization, oligomerization and further hydrolysis to formate. Any subsequent concentration toward 200 mM formamide must occur only after demonstrating retention and must not be assumed from evaporation alone.

reactions.mechanism: Atom balance: HCN + H2O -> CH3NO. Hydration of the nitrile functionality gives formamide. Productive accumulation requires stopping before substantial further amide hydrolysis or other loss.
reactions.reasoning: Speculative as an environmental supply module in this network: the transformation is chemically conventional, but the supplied Asn research does not provide a measured formamide accumulation rate or demonstrate a 200 mM reservoir produced this way. Munegumi (2014) establishes the relevance of a 200 mM formamide feed to contact-glow Asn formation, not its geochemical origin. This edge is retained only as an explicitly testable alternative to boundary-delivered formamide, and pathways using it inherit that uncertainty.

reactions.name: Alanine/formamide contact-glow Asn detection: atom-balanced observational macroedge

conditions.temperature: 300-330 K bulk-liquid screening range proposed for environmental comparison; the supplied summary does not specify the experimental bulk temperature
conditions.pressure: Ambient-pressure plasma-liquid interface; exact apparatus pressure is not supplied
conditions.other: Reported feed concentrations: 100 mM alanine and 200 mM formamide in aqueous contact-glow discharge electrolysis. No mineral catalyst is required. Experimental pH, current density, voltage and exposure duration are not given in the supplied research and must be recovered from the primary protocol rather than invented. Use time-resolved product analysis and separately cooled, optically sheltered collection. Natural lightning is only a proposed analogue, not an established equivalent.

reactions.mechanism: Formal product-channel balance: C3H7NO2 + CH3NO -> C4H8N2O3 + H2. The plasma-liquid interface drives unresolved radical and ionic chemistry that produces Asn within a mixture. This balance does not establish direct single-step carbamoylation of alanine, atom provenance or measured H2 evolution.
reactions.reasoning: Munegumi, Shimoyama and Harada (1997) reported this abiotic product family, and Munegumi (2014) reported 3.0% Asn yield based on consumed alanine with 100 mM alanine and 200 mM formamide. That denominator is not an overall feedstock carbon yield. The edge has direct target-detection support but an unresolved microscopic mechanism. Concentrated substrates, engineered electrical geometry and unknown compatibility with crude Strecker hydrolysates limit environmental integration. No mineral catalyst or natural-lightning yield is inferred.

reactions.name: Competing Asn deamidation to aspartic acid

conditions.temperature: 300-370 K for loss measurements; proposed preservation receiver at 300-310 K
conditions.other: Measure loss at the actual pH, salinity and temperature of each receiving solution. Initial preservation screening uses pH 5.5-7.0 and optical shelter; this is a design choice, not a demonstrated stability optimum. Avoid prolonged hot storage. A provisional 90% hydrolytic-retention criterion is kdeamidation * residence_time <= 0.1053 under verified first-order kinetics. Photochemical and other losses require additional terms.

reactions.mechanism: Atom balance: C4H8N2O3 + H2O -> C4H7NO4 + NH3. Net hydrolysis replaces the side-chain carboxamide with a carboxyl group. This edge represents free-Asn deamidation and does not assign peptide-specific succinimide or isoaspartyl rate constants to the free amino acid.
reactions.reasoning: Glavin et al. (2024) emphasize the vulnerability of Asn to hot-water treatment and motivate room-temperature extraction and preservation. The supplied evidence does not provide rate constants applicable to this network. Quantitative evaluation must therefore measure kdeamidation rather than omit the sink or assign an invented lifetime. For a receiving reservoir, require J006 + J007 + J011 > kloss*[Asn], with all formation fluxes expressed per reservoir volume and kloss including hydrolysis, photolysis and export. The 90% retention inequality is a mathematical design criterion, not reported experimental performance.

pathways.name: Delivered nitriles through the aminodinitrile core
pathways.description: Boundary feedstocks are cyanoacetylene, HCN, ammonia and water. This is the most directly literature-anchored mechanistic family. The hydrolysis edge retains the experimentally supported aggregate transformation without inventing a proven sequence of positional hydrolysis intermediates. Product retention must be evaluated against rxn_012.

pathways.name: Reduced-gas supply of both nitriles followed by aqueous assembly
pathways.description: Methane and ammonia feed the separate formal HCN and cyanoacetylene source channels; water receives the products for the aminodinitrile sequence. rxn_001 and rxn_002 are parallel precursor-supply operations, not consecutive conversions of one product into the other. Atmospheric production and aqueous Asn chemistry have separate literature support, but collection, cooling and integrated yield are not demonstrated.

pathways.name: Acetylene cyanation with boundary-delivered HCN
pathways.description: Boundary feedstocks are acetylene, sufficient HCN for both cyanation and aminodinitrile formation, ammonia and water. Atmospheric cyanation supplies cyanoacetylene before aqueous assembly. This route differs from P1 in the carbon-chain precursor and inherits the conditional radical-source and atmospheric-collection assumptions of rxn_003.

pathways.name: Methane-derived HCN coupled to acetylene cyanation
pathways.description: Boundary feedstocks are methane, ammonia, acetylene and water. rxn_001 explicitly supplies the HCN needed in both rxn_003 and rxn_005, with the source reaction scaled accordingly. This avoids an unspecified HCN source but does not establish quantitative atmospheric retention or hydrolysis selectivity.

pathways.name: Reduced-gas Miller-type observational route
pathways.description: Methane, ammonia and water, with externally supplied background H2 and electrical energy, generate an Asn-containing mixture. This directly reproduces the feedstock logic of Jiang et al. (2014), not a resolved microscopic pathway. The formal H2 balance is not a measured gas inventory. Subsequent cooling and rxn_012 loss measurements are required before claiming accumulation.

pathways.name: Delivered alanine and formamide under contact-glow discharge
pathways.description: Boundary-delivered alanine and formamide are supplied at the reported 100 mM and 200 mM concentrations. This is the experimentally demonstrated contact-glow feedstock route, although natural availability of that concentrated mixture and equivalence to lightning remain unresolved. No elementary carbon-chain extension mechanism is asserted.

pathways.name: Delivered alanine with HCN-derived formamide
pathways.description: Boundary feedstocks are alanine, HCN and water. HCN hydration supplies formamide before the contact-glow step. This is a conditional feedstock-origin alternative to P6: accumulation of sufficient formamide, avoidance of further hydrolysis and attainment of the reported discharge-feed concentrations have not been demonstrated.

pathways.name: Strecker-derived alanine with delivered formamide
pathways.description: Boundary feedstocks are acetaldehyde, HCN, ammonia, water and formamide. The aminonitrile is hydrolyzed before formamide is added, then the cooled alanine-containing solution must be shown capable of reaching a compatible contact-glow feed composition. Established precursor chemistry and demonstrated Asn detection do not by themselves establish the integrated route.

pathways.name: Split HCN inventory supplying both alanine and formamide
pathways.description: Boundary feedstocks are acetaldehyde, HCN, ammonia and water. Separate HCN portions supply the Strecker branch and the formamide hydration branch; the sequence list is a topological ordering of those branches. They converge only after separate processing and characterization. The formamide supply and compatibility of the combined crude solutions remain unvalidated.

pathways.name: Methane-derived HCN feeding the dual-precursor contact-glow route
pathways.description: Boundary feedstocks are methane, ammonia, acetaldehyde and water. rxn_001 explicitly supplies HCN to both the alanine and formamide branches, with sufficient source throughput for each. This is the most integrated contact-glow variant but also inherits the most unmeasured delivery, concentration and mixture-compatibility requirements. It is a testable network hypothesis, not a demonstrated end-to-end environmental synthesis.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: This is the strongest mechanistically supported route, consistent with Sanchez, Ferris and Orgel (1966) and Lemmon (1970). The network correctly specifies Asn connectivity. The reversed monoamide drawn in the supplied research summary is not Asn and should not be treated as structural evidence. The remaining bottleneck is establishing the hydrolysis window that produces the correct monoamide before further conversion to Asp.
suggestions: Provide temperature, pH, concentration and reaction-time records for the addition and hydrolysis stages, distinguishing reported conditions from proposed screening conditions.
Verify the hydrolysis product against authentic Asn and the reversed monoamide, and measure time-resolved dinitrile, Asn and Asp concentrations.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Reduced-gas production of HCN and cyanoacetylene is supported by the supplied discharge literature, with conditional environmental support from Wogan et al. (2023). The source equations are acceptable formal balances, not experimentally established product distributions. Atmospheric production followed by aqueous collection is physically reasonable, but nitrile delivery, concentration, cooling and crude-mixture compatibility have not been demonstrated together with the Asn-forming core.
suggestions: Specify gas composition, energy input, nitrile production rates and collection efficiencies for the selected reducing episode.
Test collected discharge products directly in the aqueous core and quantify competing consumption and Asn degradation.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: The aqueous core is supported, but rxn_003 remains a conditional source channel. Wogan et al. (2023) supports acetylene reacting with CN radicals, not an unactivated acetylene-plus-HCN elementary reaction. HCN activation and hydrogen termination can rationalize the balanced macroequation, but their rates and competing channels are unspecified. The pathway also requires separate HCN allocations for cyanoacetylene production and rxn_005.
suggestions: Document the energy source and radical chemistry connecting HCN to CN, including the assumptions behind net hydrogen termination.
Budget at least two HCN equivalents per cyanoacetylene-derived target molecule before accounting for losses, and measure cyanoacetylene collection efficiency.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Methane-derived HCN provides a credible upstream supply, but it does not independently validate the acetylene cyanation macroedge. The central uncertainties are CN generation, cyanoacetylene survival and delivery of sufficient residual HCN to the aqueous addition stage. No conservation violation is present. Comparable confidence to P3 reflects the shared chemical bottleneck rather than a penalty for the additional source reaction.
suggestions: Couple the HCN-production and cyanation flux models so that HCN consumption by rxn_003 does not exhaust the inventory needed by rxn_005.
Specify atmospheric and aqueous residence times within Surface and demonstrate transfer into an Asn-preserving hydrolysis window.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Jiang et al. (2014) provides direct Asn detection in reduced-gas discharge products, supporting target formation without resolving its mechanism. The network correctly labels rxn_007 as observational rather than elementary. However, the reported experiment used supplied H2, an 80°C water reservoir, prolonged discharge and repeated gas replenishment; these operating conditions are not specified in the submitted reaction record. The formal equation does not establish an H2 yield.
suggestions: Record the complete experimental gas inventory, including supplied H2, separately from the reduced formal product-channel equation.
Measure absolute Asn yield and its formation-versus-destruction time course in the collector rather than extrapolating from relative chromatographic abundance.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Munegumi and co-workers provide direct experimental support for Asn formation by contact-glow discharge, including the reported 3.0% yield based on consumed alanine at 100 mM alanine and 200 mM formamide. This supports an observational product edge, not a resolved atom-transfer mechanism or measured H2 coproduct. Environmental confidence is lower because comparable solute concentrations and plasma-liquid energy coupling have not been demonstrated in the proposed surface setting.
suggestions: Specify the discharge configuration, electrical dose, solution composition and thermal history required to reproduce the reported result.
Demonstrate both feedstock concentration and an appropriate natural energy-coupling analogue before assigning a geochemical production flux.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: HCN hydration to formamide is chemically possible and balanced, but the supplied evidence does not establish a sufficiently productive supply under specified surface conditions. Calling rxn_010 conditional is appropriate; it does not establish its rate or selectivity. The measured alanine/formamide discharge result cannot establish this complete pathway without demonstrating formamide accumulation, survival and compatibility with the downstream experiment.
suggestions: Establish HCN-to-formamide kinetics and selectivity at specified pH, temperature and residence time, including competing HCN losses and further formamide hydrolysis.
Test whether the resulting solution supplies sufficient formamide to reproduce Asn formation without assuming unvalidated purification or concentration.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Acetaldehyde Strecker chemistry followed by aminonitrile hydrolysis is a sound route to alanine, and the final discharge edge has direct product evidence. The unresolved issue is compatibility of the alanine-containing hydrolysate with contact-glow synthesis: residual cyanide, ammonium, salts and hydrolysis conditions can alter discharge chemistry. Staged processing is permissible, but the required conditioning and concentration have not been demonstrated.
suggestions: Specify the aminonitrile hydrolysis conditions and any subsequent cooling, pH adjustment or concentration before discharge.
Compare Asn yields from crude Strecker hydrolysate and purified alanine under otherwise identical contact-glow conditions.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: The split-inventory design is stoichiometrically coherent: separate HCN portions can supply the alanine nitrile carbon and formamide. Sharing this feedstock is neither an advantage nor a defect by itself. Confidence is limited by the unvalidated formamide-production rate and by combining differently processed precursor solutions at concentrations suitable for contact-glow chemistry. Direct Asn evidence applies to the final prepared mixture, not yet to this integrated route.
suggestions: Provide separate HCN allocation, conversion and loss budgets for the Strecker and formamide branches.
Demonstrate that combining the branch outputs preserves adequate alanine/formamide concentrations and discharge-compatible solution chemistry.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: The added reduced-gas HCN source is chemically credible, but it does not remove the formamide-supply and plasma-interface bottlenecks shared with P9. A complete implementation must connect atmospheric HCN production and collection to two precursor-processing branches and then to an experimentally compatible discharge mixture. The uncertainty concerns flux and mixture compatibility, not the number of reactions or environments.
suggestions: Connect HCN production, collection and branch consumption through a quantitative inventory model, including volatilization and photochemical losses.
Validate rxn_010 independently, then perform an end-to-end experiment using realistic collected and processed mixtures.

evaluation.network_feedback: The complete network has sufficient nodes, consistent molecule IDs and a connected graph with no isolated subgraphs. The deterministic check establishes conservation for all 12 reactions: seven balance as written and five with reasonable coefficients. There are no UNBALANCED reactions, and the problematic-reaction lists identify evidentiary or operating-condition gaps, not conservation failures. Boundary-delivered intermediates are acceptable as explicitly declared. Literature alignment is strong: the aminodinitrile core has the clearest mechanistic support, and the two discharge branches appropriately distinguish observed Asn formation from established elementary mechanisms or closed material balances. The target connectivity is correct, and unspecified stereochemistry requires no enantioselective step. The ten variants are not ten independent demonstrations and receive no numerical-diversity bonus. The principal network limitations are conditional CN-mediated cyanoacetylene supply in rxn_003, insufficiently specified formamide supply in rxn_010, selective hydrolysis in rxn_006, and unvalidated concentration, collection and crude-mixture compatibility. Labeling every stage Surface is not intrinsically inconsistent, but does not replace reaction-specific temperature, pH, residence-time and energy-coupling records; the mechanism and numerical-condition fields mentioned in the strategy are not included in the submitted reaction list. Reaction-level literature references should also be attached explicitly. The degradation sink rxn_012 is chemically sound, with a reaction score of 0.94, but its inclusion does not establish loss rates or net accumulation. Overall, this is a credible, literature-informed synthesis proposal rather than a validated integrated environmental process. It is not APPROVED at the network threshold of 0.90; pathway approvals above use the separately requested threshold of 0.80.
